# Tag

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 2 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a topic, a category or a keyword on the thing it describes, usually several in a
wrapping row. For a status such as Paid or Overdue, use a Badge.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Tag>Design systems</Tag>
  <Tag tone="info">Accessibility</Tag>
</div>
```

Tag has no ARIA role, so the text must carry the meaning; colour alone never does. This is
the server half: the removable tag and its dismiss button arrive with the client half.

## Long labels

A Tag stays on one line and never grows wider than its container. Plain text is cut with an
ellipsis; an element passed as the label (`<strong>`, a translation component) is clipped
at the edge of the chip, with no ellipsis.

In a row that does not wrap, a Tag keeps its width, as a Badge does. Add `className="shrink"`
and it shrinks and truncates instead.

## A linked tag

Make the link the chip, and give the label a span of its own so it keeps the ellipsis:

```tsx
<Link href="/topics/react" className={tagVariants()}>
  <span className="truncate min-w-0">React</span>
</Link>
```

Add your own focus ring and touch target to the link; `dummy/link.tsx` shows both. Do not put
a link inside a Tag: its focus ring is cut off at size `xs` and at the end of a long label.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Tag } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The label, and any icon beside it. The text carries the meaning; colour never does alone. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The shared size scale; custom emits no size classes. |
| `tone` | no | `primary` \| `neutral` \| `success` \| `warning` \| `danger` \| `info` | `"neutral"` | The meaning it signals, which picks the soft tint and its label colour. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
